chosen.title: The Robot That Dreams First: How World Models Are Teaching Machines to Imagine Before They Move
chosen.rationale: World foundation models are the hottest frontier in robotics right now — Google DeepMind shipped Gemini Robotics 2 (July 30, 2026) and NVIDIA's open Cosmos 3 omni-model lets robots simulate outcomes in a closed loop before acting. It's a pure mechanism story (how a machine 'imagines' physics before it moves) with grounded optimism and honest limits — exactly Kenji's wheelhouse, and distinct from AIMA's existing humanoid-IPO and factory-floor pieces.

rejected_candidates.title: Breaking the Rare-Earth Curse: How AI Found 25 New Magnets That Could Set the Electric Car Free
rejected_candidates.rationale: A University of New Hampshire team used AI to build a 67,573-compound magnetic database and surface 25 new rare-earth-free magnets that hold up at high temperature (Nature Communications) — landing straight into 2026's rare-earth supply-chain anxiety. Materials science + clean energy + geopolitics, with a hopeful-but-skeptical arc; distinct from #29's autonomous-lab method piece because it's about the outcome and the stakes, not the lab.

rejected_candidates.title: The Machines Building the Solar Farm: Inside the Robots Learning to Construct Clean Energy
rejected_candidates.rationale: Gritt exited stealth with $32M (TechCrunch, July 21, 2026) to build robots that assemble solar plants — a fresh, sensory, boots-in-the-dirt robotics-meets-climate story that isn't another warehouse-humanoid piece. Perfect for Kenji: a specific frontier (autonomous construction in the field), a real mechanism, and an honest reckoning about labor and buildout speed.
